title: SimpleMemVLA: A Simple but Effective Native-Video Memory for Vision-Language-Action Models
abstract: Long-horizon manipulation is partially observable: the information needed to choose the next action may appear only in observations from minutes earlier. Existing memory mechanisms for VLAs, such as retrieval banks, learned compressors and recurrent states, must decide what to keep from the past before knowing what a future decision will require. They were motivated by the assumption that minute-scale history is too large to process directly, which no longer holds for modern VLM backbones. We propose SimpleMemVLA, a VLA without a dedicated memory module that uses the backbone's native video context directly as memory. It keeps the sampled history intact in the timestamped video format the backbone was pretrained to process, routes the evidence it finds to a standard flow-matching action head through the hidden states of a generated sub-task, and prefills the history shared by consecutive decisions during action execution, keeping latency close to that of a single-frame VLA. SimpleMemVLA achieves state-of-the-art results on four memory benchmarks without loss on general-purpose control, and with the same backbone and training setup it outperforms retrieval, compression and recurrent-state methods by a wide margin. History interventions show that the policy reads specific evidence from its past and follows edited histories without parameter updates, a visual form of in-context learning. On a physical dual-arm robot, it completes two tasks whose decisive evidence disappears before the robot acts. Code available at this https URL

segments.speaker: John
segments.en: Welcome to Advanced Topics in Embodied AI. Today's lecture is on 'SIMPLEMEMVLA: A SIMPLE BUT EFFECTIVE NATIVE-VIDEO MEMORY FOR VISION-LANGUAGE-ACTION MODELS.' We've seen a lot of recent work, like 'MemoryVLA' and 'EventVLA,' focusing on engineering sophisticated, dedicated memory modules for robots to handle long-horizon tasks. This paper, primarily from researchers at Huazhong University of Science and Technology and Tsinghua University, challenges that trend. It asks a simple question: what if the VLM backbone itself is already a sufficient memory mechanism? Go ahead, Noah?
segments.zh: 欢迎来到具身智能进阶专题。今天这节课讲的是《SIMPLEMEMVLA：一种简单但有效的视觉-语言-动作模型原生视频记忆》。最近我们看到了很多工作，比如《MemoryVLA》和《EventVLA》，都在专注于为机器人设计精巧、专用的记忆模块，以处理长时程任务。而这篇论文，主要来自华中科技大学和清华大学的研究人员，对这一趋势提出了挑战。它问了一个很简单的问题：如果VLM主干本身就已经是一个足够好的记忆机制呢？诺亚，你来说？

segments.speaker: Noah
segments.en: Excuse me, Professor. So the core idea is to just get rid of the memory module entirely and feed the model a long video stream?
segments.zh: 不好意思，教授。所以核心思路就是完全去掉记忆模块，直接给模型喂一段长视频流？

segments.speaker: John
segments.en: Precisely. The central problem this paper identifies with existing approaches—be it retrieval banks, learned compressors, or recurrent states—is something they call 'write-time commitment.' This means the model has to decide what information to save, compress, or abstract from the past before it knows what will be needed for a future action. If it guesses wrong, critical information is lost. For example, a robot might not think the color of a block is important when it first sees it, but then be asked to retrieve the 'red block' two minutes later after it's been covered.
segments.zh: 正是如此。这篇论文指出现有方法——无论是检索库、学习到的压缩器，还是循环状态——的核心问题，在于一种他们称为“写入时承诺”的现象。也就是说，模型必须在还不知道未来动作需要什么信息的时候，就决定要从过去保存、压缩或抽象哪些内容。一旦判断失误，关键信息就丢了。举个例子，机器人第一次看到某个积木时可能觉得颜色不重要，但两分钟后积木被盖住了，它却被要求去拿“红色积木”。

segments.speaker: Noah
segments.en: And that information would be gone in a compressed memory.
segments.zh: 而这些信息在压缩后的记忆里就消失了。

segments.speaker: John
segments.en: Exactly. SimpleMemVLA's main contribution is to argue that this commitment is no longer necessary. Modern VLM backbones have massive context windows—hundreds of thousands of tokens. The authors calculated that a minute of video history, sampled at a typical rate, only uses a small fraction of that context. So instead of abstracting history, they just feed a raw, timestamped video stream directly to the model. The model's self-attention mechanism can then decide what's important at 'read-time'—that is, at the moment it needs to make a decision, informed by the current prompt and observation.
segments.zh: 没错。SimpleMemVLA 的核心贡献就在于论证这种取舍已经不再必要了。现代 VLM 主干网络拥有超大的上下文窗口——动辄几十万个 token。作者算过，一分钟的视频历史，按典型采样率来算，只占其中很小一部分。所以与其对历史做抽象压缩，他们干脆把带时间戳的原始视频流直接喂给模型。模型的注意力机制可以在“读取时”决定什么重要——也就是在它需要做决策的那一刻，结合当前的提示和观测来判断。

segments.speaker: Noah
segments.en: But doesn't processing a minute of video at every single step create a huge latency problem for real-time control?
segments.zh: 但每一步都要处理一分钟的视频，这难道不会给实时控制带来严重的延迟问题吗？

segments.speaker: John
segments.en: That's the critical engineering challenge they address, and it brings us to their methodology. They have a three-part approach. First, as we discussed, is retaining the raw history in the model's native video format. Second, and this is quite clever, is how they connect that history to the action. The VLM backbone doesn't directly output an action. Instead, it generates a short textual description of the current sub-task, like 'picking up the red block.' This text acts as a compact, narrow channel of information.
segments.zh: 这正是他们要解决的关键工程难题，也引出了他们的方法。他们采用了一个三部分的方案。第一，就像我们讨论过的，把原始历史保留在模型原生的视频格式里。第二，这一点相当巧妙，就是他们如何把这段历史和动作连接起来。VLM主干并不直接输出动作，而是生成一段对当前子任务的简短文字描述，比如“拿起红色方块”。这段文字充当了一个紧凑、狭窄的信息通道。

segments.speaker: Noah
segments.en: Wait, so all the rich visual information from the past minute gets distilled down into a single sentence?
segments.zh: 等等，所以过去一分钟里所有丰富的视觉信息都被浓缩成了一句话？

segments.speaker: John
segments.en: The sentence itself isn't the only information. A separate action head conditions its decision on the contextual hidden states and token embeddings associated with that generated text. The key finding from their ablations is that the hidden states carry most of the crucial, history-dependent signal. It acts as a kind of working memory that the backbone writes to at each step, informed by its full attention over the visual history. This separates the large-scale perception problem from the low-level control problem.
segments.zh: 这句话本身并不是唯一的信息。还有一个独立的动作头，它会根据与生成文本相关的上下文隐藏状态和token嵌入来做决策。他们通过消融实验得到的关键发现是，隐藏状态承载了大部分关键的、依赖历史的信号。它就像一种工作记忆，骨干网络在每一步都会写入其中，而写入的内容则来自它对整个视觉历史的完整注意力。这样一来，就把大规模感知问题和底层控制问题分开了。

segments.speaker: Noah
segments.en: Okay, that makes sense. But what about the latency? How do they solve that?
segments.zh: 好，这说得通。但延迟问题呢？他们是怎么解决的？

segments.speaker: John
segments.en: This is their third component: exact streaming inference. The insight here is that from one decision step to the next, most of the video history is shared. So, while the robot is physically executing the last action chunk, the system 'prefills' the key-value cache for the shared portion of the history. When it's time for the next decision, it only needs to process the small amount of new video data that has arrived. This overlaps computation with execution, and they showed it reduces decision latency from over a second to under 700 milliseconds, which is fast enough for real-time control.
segments.zh: 这是他们的第三个组件：精确的流式推理。这里的洞见在于，从一个决策步到下一个决策步，大部分视频历史是共享的。所以，当机器人正在物理执行上一个动作块时，系统会为共享的那部分历史“预填充”键值缓存。等到该做下一个决策时，它只需要处理新到达的那一小部分视频数据。这就把计算和执行重叠了起来，他们证明这能把决策延迟从超过一秒降到700毫秒以下，快到足以支撑实时控制。

segments.speaker: John
segments.en: The implications of this work are significant. It fundamentally reframes the memory problem in robotics. Instead of asking 'how do we build a better memory module?', it asks 'how can we best leverage the memory already inherent in our foundation models?' Their results on benchmarks like RoboMME and RoboMemArena are state-of-the-art, substantially outperforming methods with dedicated memory modules. This suggests that for many tasks, the bottleneck wasn't the model's capacity, but the information loss from premature abstraction.
segments.zh: 这项工作的意义很重大。它从根本上重新定义了机器人领域的记忆问题。不再是问“我们怎么造一个更好的记忆模块”，而是问“我们怎么才能最好地利用基础模型里本来就有的记忆？”他们在RoboMME和RoboMemArena这些基准上的结果达到了当前最优，大幅超越了那些专门设计了记忆模块的方法。这说明对很多任务来说，瓶颈并不在模型容量，而在于过早抽象带来的信息损失。

segments.speaker: Noah
segments.en: So how does this compare to a retrieval-based method like MemER? That also uses past experiences.
segments.zh: 那这和MemER这种基于检索的方法比起来怎么样？它同样也利用了过去的经验。

segments.speaker: John
segments.en: Good question. MemER and other retrieval methods still operate on a form of write-time commitment. The system has to first decide which experiences to save to its database. Then, at runtime, a retrieval mechanism has to select which of those saved snippets are relevant. SimpleMemVLA avoids both steps. It just keeps the immediate, continuous raw history available. The ablation studies in the paper are quite telling: when they implemented a retrieval-based memory on the same backbone, performance on the RoboMME benchmark dropped from 88 percent down to about 31 percent. That directly isolates the benefit of preserving the raw, temporally ordered context.
segments.zh: 这个问题问得好。MemER和其他检索方法本质上还是得在写入时就做决定。系统得先决定哪些经验存进数据库，然后在运行时，还得靠一个检索机制去挑出哪些存下来的片段是相关的。SimpleMemVLA把这两步都省了，它只是把最近这段连续的原始历史一直保留着。论文里的消融实验很能说明问题：他们在同一个主干网络上换成基于检索的记忆，RoboMME基准上的表现就从88%掉到了大概31%。这就直接分离出了保留原始、按时间排序的上下文到底带来了多大的好处。

segments.speaker: Noah
segments.en: And they showed the model was actually using the memory, right? Not just succeeding for other reasons?
segments.zh: 而且他们证明了模型确实在用记忆，对吧？不是靠别的原因才成功的？

segments.speaker: John
segments.en: Yes, their causal intervention experiments are a highlight. They would mask or even replace parts of the video history and observe the policy's behavior change accordingly. For example, splicing in a video of a red block being picked up would cause the robot to try and pick up a red block. This demonstrates an emergent form of visual in-context learning, which is a powerful capability.
segments.zh: 是的，他们的因果干预实验是一大亮点。他们会遮蔽甚至替换部分视频历史，然后观察策略的行为如何相应改变。比如，拼接一段拿起红色方块的视频，就会让机器人也去尝试拿起红色方块。这展示了一种涌现出来的视觉上下文学习能力，是一种非常强大的能力。

segments.speaker: John
segments.en: In summary, SimpleMemVLA makes a compelling case that for long-horizon manipulation, the most effective memory might be the simplest one: the raw video feed itself. By avoiding the pitfalls of early commitment and leveraging the vast context windows of modern VLMs, it achieves superior performance with a less complex architecture. The key takeaway is that native context should now be considered the default baseline. Any new, complex memory mechanism must first prove it can outperform just giving the model direct access to its own history. Thanks for listening. If you have any further questions, ask our AI assistant or drop a comment.
segments.zh: 总之，SimpleMemVLA 提出了一个很有说服力的观点：对于长时程操作任务来说，最有效的记忆可能就是最简单的那个——原始视频流本身。通过避免过早承诺的陷阱，并利用现代 VLM 庞大的上下文窗口，它以更简单的架构实现了更优的性能。关键结论是，原生上下文现在应该被视为默认基线。任何新的、复杂的记忆机制，都必须首先证明它能超越直接让模型访问自身历史这一做法。感谢收听。如果还有任何问题，可以问我们的 AI 助手，或者留言评论。
